name: Abu Dhabi
tagline: Stately capital of mosques, museums and quiet luxury.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: November to March is the only temperate window, and it holds the year's marquee season: the Grand Prix, Frieze, tennis and festival concerts; avoid the severe April-October heat that pushes well into the forties.

ourTake.lede: Abu Dhabi is the cultural and unhurried counterpoint to Dubai, and most people give it a rushed day when it deserves two. Prioritise the Louvre and the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, the mosque at dusk, when the white marble turns and the crowds thin, and leave the theme parks on Yas for travellers with children. The real luxury here is space and calm, not spectacle.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the polish of the Gulf with more calm and culture than its neighbour, and the Louvre on your doorstep.
ourTake.skipIf: You want nightlife and buzz; this is the quieter, more considered emirate.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri, Abu Dhabi

items.name: Anantara Qasr Al Sarab Desert Resort

items.description: A fortress of dunes deep in the Empty Quarter, the desert at its most cinematic.

items.name: Al Wathba, a Luxury Collection Desert Resort & Spa
items.description: A closer, gentler desert escape, dunes and a serious spa within easy reach of the city.

items.name: Saadiyat Rotana Resort & Villas
items.description: A dependable beach resort on the cultural island, generous with space.

items.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
credentials: World's largest hand-knotted carpet, 5,627 sqm, over 2.2 billion knots
items.description: The single most beautiful building in the UAE, 82 white-marble domes, more than 1,000 columns, gold-gilded chandeliers set with millions of Swarovski crystals, and reflecting pools that mirror the whole structure at dusk. Free to enter; modest dress is required and abayas are lent to women at the gate. Go late afternoon into blue hour for the light, and ask a private guide to time the visit around prayer hours so the family has the marble courtyards nearly to themselves.

items.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
credentials: First universal museum in the Arab world
items.description: Jean Nouvel's masterwork, a 180-metre latticed dome that filters the sun into a shifting 'rain of light' over galleries that tell one connected story of humanity, from ancient civilisations to Monet and Da Vinci. The building alone is worth the trip. Book a private after-hours or curator-led tour, and end with a table on the water at Fouquet's or Aptitude for the dome lit against the Gulf.

items.name: Qasr Al Watan
items.description: The working presidential palace, opened to the public, not a former royal home but the seat of the UAE state, all white stone, mother-of-pearl and one of the largest domes in the world above a hall lit by a 350,000-crystal chandelier. The Presidential Gifts collection and the House of Knowledge give older children and grandparents a genuine sense of the nation. Stay for the evening 'Palace in Motion' light-and-sound show projected on the façade.

items.name: teamLab Phenomena Abu Dhabi
credentials: World's largest digital-art museum, opened April 2025
items.description: The world's largest digital-art space, 17,000 sqm of immersive, ever-changing rooms where light, water and air become the artwork and no two visits are the same. It is pure wonder for every generation, from a five-year-old to a grandparent, and the most photographed new opening in the city. Book a timed slot well ahead; it sells out, and a weekday morning is calmest for a multi-gen group.

items.name: Zayed National Museum
credentials: Opened December 2025, designed by Foster + Partners
items.description: The national museum of the UAE, newly opened, under Norman Foster's five soaring falcon-wing steel towers, 1,500 objects across six galleries tracing the country from its earliest human habitation to the vision of founder Sheikh Zayed. The clearest, most dignified window into Emirati history and identity, and a natural anchor for a Saadiyat culture day. A private guide brings the story alive for teenagers.

items.name: Emirates Palace (Mandarin Oriental)
items.description: A palace-hotel of gold-leaf domes and a kilometre of private beach, one of the grandest addresses in the region even if you are not staying. Come for the famous 24-carat-gold-flaked cappuccino and camel-milk high tea in Le Vendôme, walk the marble halls, and watch the domes turn amber at sunset. Discreet, cavernous and cool, an easy, elegant afternoon for a family in the heat.

items.name: The Corniche & Corniche Beach
items.description: Eight kilometres of landscaped waterfront promenade fronting the Gulf, the city's front lawn, with a Blue Flag beach, shaded cycle paths, playgrounds and calm swimming water. Best at golden hour when families walk the seawall and the skyline lights up across the bay. Rent bikes for the older children, or book a majlis cabana for a low-key, sun-safe afternoon.

items.name: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
credentials: Guinness World Record, fastest rollercoaster launch (Formula Rossa)
items.description: The world's first Ferrari-branded park, under a vast red roof, built around Formula Rossa, the ride that fires you from 0 to 240 km/h in under five seconds, still the record-holder for fastest rollercoaster launch. There are gentler Cavallino and Junior GT rides for younger children too, so a thrill-seeking teen and a cautious grandparent can share the day. Book Fast Track to skip the queues.

items.name: Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi
credentials: Among the world's largest indoor theme parks
items.description: A fully indoor, fully air-conditioned theme park across six lands of Batman, Looney Tunes, Scooby-Doo and Tom & Jerry, 29 rides and shows under one roof, which matters in the summer heat. Genuinely joyful for younger children and nostalgic parents alike, with immersive Gotham City and Cartoon Junction streets. Pair it with a Yas Island multi-park pass if the family wants more than one day.

items.name: SeaWorld Abu Dhabi
credentials: Guinness World Record, largest indoor marine-life theme park; world's largest multi-species aquarium
items.description: A next-generation marine park across five levels, home to the world's largest multi-species aquarium and a research and rescue centre at its core. More than 100,000 animals, immersive realms and animal encounters make it a standout for children, with none of the orca controversy of older parks. Book a behind-the-scenes or animal-encounter add-on for an unforgettable family morning.

items.name: Yas Waterworld
items.description: An Emirati-themed waterpark with more than 40 rides, slides and attractions, including record-setting coasters and a vast wave pool, enough range that toddlers, teenagers and adults each have their own thing. Cabana rentals and quiet lazy-river stretches keep it comfortable for a multi-gen group in the heat. A relaxed counterpoint to the high-adrenaline parks next door.

items.name: Yas Marina Circuit
credentials: Host of the Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
items.description: The Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix venue, and outside race week you can drive it yourself, take a passenger hot lap in a GT car, or cycle the floodlit track on TrainYAS evenings. The season-closing night race is one of the great sporting-and-hospitality events in the calendar, with paddock and yacht-side tables that a concierge can secure well in advance. A dream day for a car-loving family.

items.name: Qasr Al Hosn
items.description: The oldest stone building in the city, the 18th-century watchtower and fort around which Abu Dhabi grew, now a beautifully restored museum of the emirate's origins. Quiet, shaded and deeply atmospheric, with the adjacent House of Artisans keeping traditional crafts alive. A gentle, air-conditioned hour of real history between the glass towers, ideal with grandparents.

items.name: Mangrove National Park (kayaking)
items.description: A protected labyrinth of tidal channels through dense mangrove forest, just minutes from downtown, glide it by clear-bottom or standard kayak, or a guided eco-tour, and watch for herons, flamingos and darting fish. Serene, green and completely unexpected in a desert city. Book a private sunrise or sunset paddle for calm water and cool air; gentle enough for older children.

items.name: Saadiyat Beach & the turtles
items.description: A pristine, protected white-sand beach where hawksbill turtles come ashore to nest each spring, the finest stretch of coast in the emirate, fronted by the St. Regis and Park Hyatt. Book a beach-club day bed for the family, and if the season is right, ask the resort's marine team about the supervised turtle-nesting programme. Discreet luxury and genuine wildlife in one place.

items.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi, dome & waterfront at night
items.description: Beyond the galleries, the museum's outdoor plazas and the 'rain of light' under the dome are magical after dark, with the sea lapping between the buildings. A private evening kayak or paddleboard beneath the illuminated dome, arranged through the museum, is one of the most romantic and photogenic experiences in the city, and unforgettable for a couple or a family celebrating together.

items.name: Observation Deck at 300 (Etihad Towers)
items.description: The city's highest public viewpoint, on the 74th floor of Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers, a 360-degree sweep over the Corniche, Emirates Palace and the Gulf, 300 metres up. Take the afternoon-tea slot so the family enjoys pastries as the light turns and the towers glow. A calm, elevated hour that anchors the geography of the city for first-time visitors.

items.name: Heritage Village
items.description: A reconstructed traditional oasis village on the Breakwater, with a Bedouin camp, working craftsmen, potters, weavers, metalworkers, and a small museum, all facing a postcard view of the skyline across the water. Free, unhurried and hands-on, it gives children a tactile sense of pre-oil life. Best in the cooler morning, paired with the nearby Marina Mall for lunch.

items.name: Al Ain Oasis
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cultural Sites of Al Ain
items.description: A living, working oasis of 147,000 date palms fed by the ancient falaj irrigation channels, cool, green and shaded, with an eco-centre explaining 4,000 years of desert agriculture. Part of the UAE's first UNESCO site and a serene contrast to the coast. A private guide and an easy walk suit every age; combine it with the Al Ain museums for a full 'Garden City' day-trip.

items.name: Jebel Hafeet
items.description: The emirate's highest peak at 1,240 metres, reached by one of the world's great driving roads, a sweeping, beautifully engineered mountain ascent to a summit terrace with vast views over Al Ain and the desert into Oman. Go for sunset, then descend to the Mercure summit hotel or the Green Mubazzarah hot springs at the foot. A thrilling, scenic centrepiece for the Al Ain trip.

items.name: Anantara Qasr Al Sarab & the Empty Quarter
credentials: Set within the Rub' al Khali, the world's largest sand desert
items.description: A fortress-like resort rising from the towering apricot dunes of the Rub' al Khali, the Empty Quarter, the largest continuous sand desert on earth. This is the desert at its most cinematic: dune drives, camel treks, private dinners in the sand and star-filled silence. An overnight or two here is the emirate's most romantic and exclusive escape, with the discretion and service a UHNI family expects.

items.name: Sir Bani Yas Island
credentials: One of the world's largest Arabian oryx herds
items.description: A private nature island off the western coast, home to the 1,400-hectare Arabian Wildlife Park where 17,000 free-roaming animals, including one of the world's largest herds of Arabian oryx, plus giraffe, cheetah and gazelle, roam a real Sheikh Zayed rewilding project. Reached by ferry or seaplane, with three Anantara resorts, it offers safari drives, kayaking and archery. A genuine wildlife retreat, far from the crowds.

items.name: Yas Beach
items.description: A relaxed, well-run beach club on Yas Island, clean sand, calm water, day beds, watersports and easygoing food, a natural cool-down after the theme parks. Family-friendly and unpretentious, with shaded cabanas that keep grandparents and small children comfortable. Book a lounger set and let the day slow down after the adrenaline of Ferrari World.

items.name: Qasr Al Muwaiji
items.description: A restored oasis fort, the birthplace of the current UAE President, now an elegant museum wrapped in a modern glass shell that lets you walk the ramparts. Quiet, dignified and rarely crowded, it deepens the Al Ain history day with a personal royal story. A short, air-conditioned visit that pairs naturally with the oasis and museums nearby.

items.name: Al Jahili Fort
items.description: One of the UAE's largest and best-preserved forts, set in a green park, with a permanent exhibition on explorer Wilfred Thesiger's crossings of the Empty Quarter. The circular tower and palm-shaded courtyards are photogenic and calm, and the Thesiger photographs are a quiet highlight for older travellers. An unhurried stop on the Al Ain circuit.

items.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi Children's Museum & family programmes
items.description: Within the Louvre, dedicated child-scaled galleries and workshops turn a museum visit into hands-on discovery, ideal for keeping younger children engaged while the adults take the main galleries at their own pace. Book the family or bilingual tour in advance. It makes the culture district genuinely multi-generational rather than adults-only.

items.name: Mangrove Beach & the National Aquarium
credentials: Largest aquarium in the Middle East
items.description: The largest aquarium in the Middle East, at the Al Qana waterfront, ten themed zones, a walk-through ocean tunnel and animal encounters, set among restaurants and a cinema for an easy evening. Comfortable, indoor and paced for children, with plenty of veg-friendly dining nearby. A relaxed cultural-and-leisure combination away from the theme-park scale.

items.name: Falconry at the Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital
items.description: The world's largest falcon hospital, where a guided tour lets you hold a falcon, learn the deep Emirati bond with these birds, and see the veterinary care up close, a genuinely unusual, hands-on encounter with a living tradition. Educational and memorable for children and adults alike. Pre-book the tour; sessions are small and personal.

items.name: Desert safari & sunset dune drive (Al Khatim / Sweihan)
items.description: The classic golden-dune experience, a private 4x4 over the sands at Al Khatim, camel rides, falconry displays and a starlit dinner in a Bedouin-style camp, all within an hour of the city. Insist on a private, chauffeured safari with a curated menu (veg and Jain requests handled ahead) rather than the shared coach tours. Magical for a family's first taste of the desert.

items.name: Abrahamic Family House
items.description: A landmark of tolerance, a mosque, a church and a synagogue standing side by side as three equal, luminous cubes by David Adjaye, with a shared forum between them. Serene, architecturally stunning and unlike anything else in the region, it speaks to co-existence in a way that resonates deeply. A thoughtful, calming stop within the Saadiyat culture cluster.

items.name: Yas Marina & the yachts
items.description: The glamorous marina beneath the W Abu Dhabi's rippling steel canopy, superyachts, waterfront restaurants and the buzz of race weekend. Charter a private day yacht along the coast, or simply take an evening table with the F1 grandstands lit behind you. A polished, grown-up counterpoint to the family parks on the same island.

items.name: Manarat Al Saadiyat & the culture district walk
items.description: The art centre and visitor gateway to the whole Saadiyat Cultural District, rotating exhibitions, the region's leading art fairs, and the clearest orientation to what is rising around it. A civilised first stop to frame a culture-district day before the Louvre and Zayed National Museum. Check the calendar for Abu Dhabi Art and gallery openings.

items.name: Wahat Al Karama
items.description: A dignified memorial to the nation's fallen, 31 leaning aluminium tablets that lean on one another, symbolising unity, reflected in a still pool facing the Grand Mosque. Quiet, powerful and beautifully designed, it takes only twenty minutes but adds real depth. Easily paired with the mosque visit next door for a fuller morning.

items.name: Louvre-to-Corniche sunset dhow cruise
items.description: A private traditional dhow or modern yacht along the Corniche at dusk, past Emirates Palace and the illuminated skyline, with dinner served on deck, the city seen from the water it was built beside. Charter it privately with a tailored menu and it becomes a serene, celebratory evening for the whole family. Calm seas and cool air make it comfortable year-round after sunset.

items.name: CLYMB Abu Dhabi
credentials: World's tallest indoor skydiving wind tunnel
items.description: Home to the world's tallest indoor skydiving wind tunnel and one of the world's largest indoor climbing walls, high-energy, weather-proof adventure for teenagers and thrill-seeking adults. Instructor-led and safe enough for first-timers, it is a memorable half-day for an active family. Book flight or climb sessions ahead, especially on weekends.

items.name: Al Ain Zoo & the Sheikh Zayed Desert Learning Centre
items.description: A large, conservation-focused zoo at the foot of Jebel Hafeet, strong on Arabian and African species, with an award-winning learning centre on desert ecology. Spacious, shaded and paced for children, it rounds out the Al Ain family day. A gentler wildlife option than the western islands, close to the oasis and forts.

items.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi rooftop & Fouquet's / fine dining on Saadiyat
items.description: The culture district doubles as one of the city's best dining clusters, Fouquet's at the Louvre, and the Saadiyat resorts' restaurants, where a private guide can pre-arrange veg, Jain or halal menus and a quiet corner table. Ending a museum day over refined food with the dome lit on the water is the discreet luxury Abu Dhabi does so well. Book ahead for sunset seatings.

items.name: Bateen Dhow-building Yard
items.description: A working shipyard where craftsmen still build wooden dhows by hand as they have for generations, a rare, unpolished glimpse of the seafaring heritage behind the modern city. Ask a guide to arrange access; it is quiet, authentic and largely undiscovered by tourists. A short, characterful stop for travellers who want the real thread of the place.

items.name: Umm Al Emarat Park
items.description: The city's oldest park, beautifully redesigned, a botanic garden, a shaded evening theatre, a small animal barn and wide lawns that come alive after dark when families picnic in the cool. Central, relaxed and free of the theme-park scale, it is where locals actually unwind. A gentle evening for grandparents and small children between the bigger days out.

items.name: Al Qana & the waterfront district
items.description: A stylish waterfront destination gathering the National Aquarium, a modern cinema, a fitness hub and a run of good restaurants along a marina promenade, an easy, comfortable evening with something for every age. Veg and international dining is plentiful, and the setting is cooler and calmer than the malls. A relaxed base for a family's last night in the city.

items.name: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi (forthcoming)
items.description: Frank Gehry's largest Guggenheim, a dramatic cluster of stone volumes and glass cones on the Saadiyat headland, dedicated to modern and contemporary art, is nearing completion and expected to open in late 2026, completing the culture district. Worth knowing for trip-planning: a return visit once it opens will round out the finest concentration of world museums in the region. Not yet open to visitors as of mid-2026.

plan.heading: 3 days in Abu Dhabi, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive early at the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, unhurried, before the tour groups.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Check into the Emirates Palace, Mandarin Oriental, and take a long lunch on the terrace over the private beach.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Hakkasan, then the palace gardens after dark.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private morning at Louvre Abu Dhabi under Jean Nouvel's rain-of-light dome, then the new Zayed National Museum on Saadiyat.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at Fouquet's, then an afternoon on Saadiyat's protected beach where turtles nest.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Talea by Antonio Guida, and a quiet drink overlooking the marina.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive to the Liwa oasis at the edge of the Rub' al Khali, climbing Tel Moreeb by 4x4.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch and stillness at Qasr Al Sarab, a Desert Resort by Anantara set among the high dunes.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners atop a dune, then a slow dinner back at the resort under the stars.

items.name: Saadiyat Island
items.description: The cultural and beach quarter, Louvre, the new museums and the best resorts on a protected shore; for slow, design-led stays.

items.name: The Corniche / city centre
items.description: The waterfront heart with the promenade and easy reach of the mosque; suits a first visit that wants everything close.

items.name: Yas Island
items.description: Theme parks, the F1 circuit and big hotels on one engineered island, for families and race-weekend travellers, less so for quiet.

events.name: Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
events.note: The season finale at Yas Marina (3–6 December 2026), with Yasalam after-race concerts included for ticket holders.

events.name: Mubadala Abu Dhabi Open
events.note: WTA 500 women's tennis at Zayed Sports City (31 Jan–7 Feb 2026), a strong early-season field.

events.name: Al Dhafra Festival
events.note: A serious Emirati heritage festival in the Liwa region built around camel-beauty (mazayna) contests, the country's Bedouin culture, not its skyline.

events.name: Abu Dhabi Festival
events.note: The emirate's flagship classical-music and arts festival, bringing international orchestras, ballet and recitals to the capital.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Saadiyat Island suits those who want beach, the Louvre and quiet; the capital is more measured and conservative than Dubai, so dress a touch more covered, especially around the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, which requires modest attire and provides robes.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive at Abu Dhabi's Zayed International (AUH) and its new Terminal A, where fast-track and a chauffeured transfer put you on Saadiyat or the Corniche in under forty minutes.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver is the natural way to move between the islands and the desert; Saadiyat's cultural district and the Corniche are pleasant on foot in the cooler months.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: An eSIM from e& or du gives immediate 5G; wifi in the resorts and museums is strong and reliable.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The dirham (AED), dollar-pegged, with cards accepted universally; carry a little cash for the souks, and tip modestly as service is generally included.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November to March is the window: comfortable 20-28C days, ideal for the Grand Mosque and Saadiyat. Avoid July-September, when 40C-plus heat and Gulf humidity make the city an indoor affair.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, around 3.5 hours. Etihad flies it best in business and its First Apartments on the wider-body fleet; ask for the chauffeur transfer. Etihad's First lounge at AUH, with its own spa, is a strong reason to route onward journeys through Abu Dhabi.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations; routine plus hepatitis A and typhoid is enough. Among the safest cities anywhere, with negligible street crime. Desalinated tap water is safe; most drink bottled. Heat is the only genuine caution.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Very easy for vegetarian and Jain guests. Indian restaurants are plentiful and pure-veg options are well understood. Hotel kitchens prepare Jain meals readily with notice; the Indian dining rooms on the Corniche and at the major resorts are reliable.
